title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the notes on the structure at infinity of M_{g,ν}, Grothendieck is axiomatising the combinatorics of a divisor with normal crossings, in the stack/analytic sense. This is the situation of the Deligne–Mumford boundary of M̄_{g,ν}. Set D_0 = X, the ambient space. D_d is the 'normalised' d-fold stratum: points of X together with a choice of d local branches, i.e. curves with d chosen nodes. For d ≥ d', D_{d,d'} is the space of points of D_d together with a choice of d' among the d branches. There are two structure maps: D_{d,d'} → D_d, the forgetful map, which is finite étale; and the 'but' map D_{d,d'} → D_{d'}. The previous page asks for the evident compatibility squares (177) and remarks that the axiomatics makes sense in any site.

This page states a hypothesis meant to link with the 'maximal coverings' viewpoint: D_{d,d'} → D_{d'} should be a local immersion of smooth analytic spaces, or of spaces smooth over a given base. Grothendieck observes that it suffices to require this for D_{d,0} ≅ D_d → D_0 and D_{d',0} ≅ D_{d'} → D_0. The argument runs as follows.
- D_{d,0} → D_{d',0} → D_0 commutes.
- D_{d,d',0} ≅ D_{d,d'}, and D_{d,d',0} → D_{d',0} sits in a (trivially) cartesian square over D_{d,d'} → D_{d'}.
- Hence the composite D_{d,d'} → D_{d'} → X equals D_{d,d'} → D_d → X. That is a finite étale map followed by a local immersion, so it is a local immersion.
- A cancellation (two-out-of-three) argument for unramified, separated maps then gives that D_{d,d'} → D_{d'} is a local immersion.

He then notes that in the smooth or relatively smooth case this hypothesis can be phrased in a form that keeps meaning in an arbitrary site. The word is hard to read; the next page speaks of 'revêtements locaux'.

Finally:
- (178): since D_{d,0} ≅ D_d → D_0 =: X, all D_d map to X. The margin says the system D is an object of the category of objects over D_0.
- (179): one gets commutative squares D_{d,d'} → D_{d'}, D_d → X.

The next page deduces the codimension additivity, codim(D_{d,d'} → D_{d'}) = d − d', and imposes codim(D_d → X) = d. It then begins describing the branch set I_x of cardinality d via sections s_i of D_{d,1} → D_d.
errors: No mathematical error. The cancellation step tacitly uses that D_{d'} → X is unramified/separated (a local immersion), which is part of the hypothesis. This is standard and fine.
The transcription's 'D_{d',0} → D_0, et D_{d',0} → D_0' should read 'D_{d,0} → D_0 et D_{d',0} → D_0' (with D_{d,0} ≅ D_d, D_{d',0} ≅ D_{d'}).
The cartesian square shown has isomorphic vertical arrows, so its cartesianness is trivial. Its role is only to identify D_{d,d'} → D_{d'} with D_{d,d',0} → D_{d',0}.

ideas.what: Axiomatic system (D_d, D_{d,d'}) of 'normalised strata with chosen branches' of a normal crossings divisor, with finite étale forgetful maps and 'but' maps, over X = D_0
ideas.modern_name: Semi-simplicial/normalised stratification of a normal crossings divisor; boundary strata of M̄_{g,n} indexed by stable graphs with marked edges
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Théorie de Hodge II, 1971) for the normalisations D^{(n)}; Knudsen/Deligne–Mumford for the boundary of M̄_g; later Getzler–Kapranov (modular operads)
ideas.where_published: The Esquisse d'un programme discusses the 'structure à l'infini' / Teichmüller tower only informally

ideas.what: Reduction: D_{d,d'} → D_{d'} is a local immersion if D_d → X and D_{d'} → X are, by the factorisation through D_{d,d',0} and cancellation
ideas.modern_name: Two-out-of-three / cancellation property for unramified (local immersion) morphisms
ideas.where_published: EGA IV (cancellation properties for unramified morphisms / immersions), in spirit

ideas.what: Remark that the axiomatics, with 'local immersion' replaced by a covering-type condition, makes sense in an arbitrary site
ideas.modern_name: Normal crossings / log structures in a topos-theoretic setting (cf. Kato's log geometry, normal-crossings stacks)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches a site-theoretic (topos-level) axiomatisation of the stratification of a normal crossings boundary (as for M̄_{g,ν}) via objects D_d, D_{d,d'} over D_0. The sketch is meant to connect to 'revêtements maximaux'. It parallels later log-geometric and modular-operad formalisms but is stated only as a plan.
missed.quote: l'hyp. d'imm. locale est d'ailleurs [?] : celle de [revêt.?] local, qui garde un sens dans les sites
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mostly of historical interest. It is an early, independent attempt at an intrinsic, site-level description of boundary strata combinatorics of moduli stacks, but the content is standard.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine bookkeeping in an axiomatisation of normal-crossings strata: a cancellation lemma for local immersions plus the compatibility diagrams. The site-level framing is mildly interesting historically, but nothing here is a new result.
transcription_corrections: 'que D_{d',0} → D_0, et D_{d',0} → D_0' should be 'que D_{d,0} → D_0 et D_{d',0} → D_0' (with ≀≀ D_d, D_{d'} below).
The cartesian square is: top D_{d,d',0} → D_{d',0} (→ D_0), left vertical ≅ to D_{d,d'}, right vertical ≅ to D_{d'}, bottom D_{d,d'} ⟹ D_{d'}, labelled 'cart'.
'celle de nœud local' is doubtful; given the next page ('immersions locales (resp. des revêt. locaux)') it is likely 'celle de revêt. local'.
Margin probably reads: 'D est un objet (178) de la catégorie des (objets au-dessus de) D_0'.
In (179) the bottom-right X is crossed out, likely replaced by D_0.
The crossed-out fragments 'de condition d−d'' and 'D_{d,0} → D_0 et D_{d',0} → D_0' are deletions; 'limité, que' is also crossed out.
